content: 1. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of rimegepant via inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapy. If co-administered, monitor closely for adverse effects or increased drug levels. 2. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of riociguat through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition but decreases riociguat levels by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 3. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate inducer of CYP3A4. When co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates, monitor for reduced efficacy. Consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate if clinically indicated. 4. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of ripretinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration cannot be avoided, increase the ripretinib dose from 150 mg once daily to 150 mg twice daily during the co-administration period. Monitor for clinical response and tolerability. 5. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of risperidone via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 6. Ritonavir significantly increases the levels or effects of elagolix through mechanisms involving CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of toxicity. 7. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of ritonavir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition but decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 8. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of rivaroxaban by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely for reduced anticoagulant efficacy. 9. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of roflumilast by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 10. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of rolapitant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely for reduced efficacy. 11. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 12. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of ropivacaine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely for reduced anesthetic efficacy. 13. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of rosuvastatin through an unknown mechanism. Consider increasing the rosuvastatin dose and monitor closely for therapeutic response. 14. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 15. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 16. Rufinamide decreases the effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for reduced contraceptive efficacy. 17. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 18. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib topical by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely for reduced efficacy. 19. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of salmeterol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 20. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition but decreases saxagliptin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 21. Segesterone/ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of elagolix through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapy. Estrogen-containing contraceptives are expected to reduce elagolix efficacy. Advise women to use non-hormonal contraceptives during elagolix treatment and for one week after discontinuation. 22. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapy. 23. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 24. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of silodosin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6, which downregulates CYP450 activity during infection or inflammation. Use caution when co-administering with CYP substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. Monitor closely. 26. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of simvastatin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition but decreases simvastatin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 27. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of siponimod by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 28. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of sirolimus via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition but decreases sirolimus levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 29. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of sitagliptin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 32. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 33. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 34. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of sorafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 35. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of elagolix by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Dosage adjustments may be required. 37. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of sufentanil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 38. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 39. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of suvorexant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 40. Tacrolimus significantly increases the levels or effects of elagolix through mechanisms involving CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 41. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 42. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of talazoparib via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of tamsulosin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 44. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of tasimelteon by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 45. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and elagolix by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapy. 46. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Telmisartan significantly increases the levels or effects of elagolix through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 48. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition but decreases temsirolimus levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required.
